questions.prompt: An age field accepts integers from 18 to 65 inclusive. Using 2-value Boundary Value Analysis (BVA), which set of values should you test?
questions.explanation: BVA targets the exact boundaries (18, 65) and their immediate off-by-one neighbors (17, 66) where defects cluster.

questions.prompt: What is the goal of Equivalence Partitioning in black-box test design?

options.text: Divide inputs into classes expected to behave identically so one representative per class maximizes coverage with minimal redundancy

questions.explanation: Equivalence partitioning reduces redundant test cases while ensuring valid and invalid classes are covered.

questions.prompt: A pricing engine combines 4 independent rules (VIP tier, promo code, bulk quantity, free shipping). Which technique systematically ensures every combination of conditions and actions is covered?
questions.explanation: Decision tables map all relevant combinations of boolean/rule conditions to expected outcomes, exposing contradictory or missing rules.

rubric.label: Selects Decision Table for rule combinations

questions.prompt: When is Exploratory Testing most valuable relative to scripted regression tests?

options.text: Uncovering unexpected UX, edge-case, and integration bugs through time-boxed charters guided by tester intuition

questions.explanation: Session-based exploratory testing complements scripted automation by probing unscripted interactions and real user mental models.

questions.prompt: Select ALL scenarios that represent high-value negative test cases for a file upload endpoint.

options.text: Uploading a file exceeding the maximum size limit
Uploading a disguised executable renamed with a .png extension
Uploading a valid 100 KB PNG image

questions.explanation: Negative testing validates bounds, content-type/magic-byte validation, and corrupted payload handling.

rubric.label: Designs security and boundary negative tests

questions.prompt: Design a concise test charter for a client-side timed exam app that persists progress in localStorage/IndexedDB, covering at least 4 critical edge cases.
questions.explanation: Cover mid-test reload resume, timer expiry auto-submit, full/corrupted storage fallback, multi-tab concurrency, and offline reload.

questions.prompt: In Playwright E2E tests, why are user-facing locators (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`) preferred over brittle XPath or deep CSS chains?

options.text: They resist layout refactors and simultaneously verify accessible names and roles

questions.explanation: Role/label locators align tests with user perception and accessibility semantics while minimizing maintenance churn.

questions.prompt: An E2E test uses `await page.waitForTimeout(3000)` and fails intermittently in CI. What is the right fix?

options.text: Replace arbitrary sleeps with web-first auto-retrying assertions (e.g., `expect(locator).toBeVisible()`) or deterministic network/state waits

questions.explanation: Hard sleeps are slow when fast and flaky when CI is under load; condition-based waits make suites fast and deterministic.

questions.prompt: According to the Test Pyramid (or Testing Trophy), why should the majority of business-logic checks live in unit and integration tests rather than browser E2E tests?

options.text: Unit/integration tests execute in milliseconds, isolate root causes precisely, and have far lower flake and maintenance cost

questions.explanation: Reserve browser E2E for critical user journeys while covering combinatorial logic in fast, isolated unit/integration layers.

rubric.label: Optimizes CI feedback speed and signal

questions.prompt: Implement `classifyFlakyRuns(results)` that takes an array of `{ testId, passed }` run records and returns a sorted array of `testId`s that both passed at least once AND failed at least once.
questions.hint: Track per-testId booleans `{ hasPass, hasFail }` in a Map, then filter and sort.
questions.explanation: Identifies non-deterministic flaky tests by detecting mixed pass/fail outcomes across repeated runs.

questions.prompt: Select ALL practices that keep a CI Playwright suite reliable and debuggable on failure.

options.text: Upload HTML report, traces, and failure screenshots as CI artifacts
Isolate test state/storage per test so tests are order-independent
Share mutable global state across parallel workers
Pin browser and dependency versions via lockfile

questions.explanation: Isolated state, pinned toolchains, and trace/screenshot artifacts make CI failures immediately actionable.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of integrating `axe-core` into Playwright CI tests?

options.text: Automatically detect WCAG accessibility violations (contrast, ARIA, labels, landmarks) on every PR

questions.explanation: Automated axe-core checks catch ~30–50% of WCAG issues immediately in CI, complementing manual keyboard and screen-reader audits.

rubric.label: Automates WCAG baseline checks in CI

questions.prompt: A typo in the company name appears on the public checkout banner, causing zero functional breakage. How should Severity and Priority be classified?

options.text: Low Severity (S4), High Priority (P1/P2) due to brand visibility

questions.explanation: Severity measures technical/functional impact; Priority measures business urgency to fix.

questions.prompt: Which piece of information is MOST essential for a developer to fix a bug quickly without back-and-forth?

options.text: Minimal deterministic steps to reproduce, expected vs actual result, environment/version, and logs/screenshot
Guessing which line of code is wrong without repro steps

questions.explanation: Actionable defect reports eliminate ambiguity and cut mean time to resolution dramatically.

rubric.label: Includes environment and expected vs actual

questions.prompt: Two hours before release, QA discovers that exporting a PDF crashes the browser tab with an uncaught exception. What is the correct triage severity and release action?

options.text: S1/S2 High-Critical blocker — hold release (No-Go) until fixed or scoped out with stakeholder sign-off
S4 Cosmetic — ship without mentioning it

questions.explanation: Uncaught crashes on a core deliverable violate Go/No-Go quality gates and require a fix or explicit leadership waiver.

questions.prompt: A developer marks a bug "Cannot Reproduce". What should QA do next?

options.text: Verify environment parity (browser, build SHA, data state, feature flags), attach HAR/trace/video, and pair briefly to reproduce
Reopen 10 times with no new info

questions.explanation: Environment/data drift causes most "cannot reproduce" loops; concrete traces and pairing resolve them fast.

questions.prompt: Write a structured S2 bug report for an assessment timer that resets to full duration when the user refreshes the page mid-test.
questions.explanation: Include title, severity S2, exact repro steps, expected resumed countdown, actual reset behavior, and impact on exam integrity.

rubric.label: States expected vs actual and impact

questions.prompt: What is Defect Escape Rate (or Defect Leakage), and what does an upward trend indicate?

options.text: Percentage of defects found in production vs caught before release; a rising rate signals gaps in test coverage or release gates
Number of bugs closed per day
Count of unit tests per file

questions.explanation: Tracking escaped defects guides where to strengthen unit, integration, or UAT coverage.

rubric.label: Uses metrics to improve test strategy

questions.prompt: When a hotfix touches only the payment webhook handler with 30 minutes before deploy, which test subset should run first?

options.text: Targeted smoke + risk-based regression on payment/checkout flows plus full automated CI unit/API checks
Manual testing of the About Us page only
A 3-day full manual regression before any CI

questions.explanation: Risk-based regression focuses limited time on impacted modules and critical revenue paths backed by automated CI.

rubric.label: Protects critical paths under time pressure

questions.prompt: What is the difference between Confirmation Testing (re-testing) and Regression Testing?

options.text: Confirmation testing verifies the specific bug fix works; regression testing verifies the fix did not break existing unaffected functionality
Regression testing only runs on new features
Confirmation testing never uses test data

questions.explanation: Both are required: confirm the fix resolves the defect, then verify no collateral side effects occurred.

questions.prompt: How should QA manage visual regression baselines (e.g., Playwright screenshots) to prevent noisy false positives?

options.text: Run in a consistent OS/browser container, mask dynamic timestamps/animations, and review intentional UI diffs in PRs
Compare screenshots across random developer laptops

questions.explanation: Deterministic rendering environments and masking dynamic elements keep visual diffs high-signal.

questions.prompt: Select ALL valid triggers for executing a full cross-browser regression pass.

options.text: Major dependency or framework upgrade (e.g., router/bundler)
Database schema or persistence layer overhaul
Core authentication or scoring engine refactor

questions.explanation: High-blast-radius infrastructure and core-engine changes warrant full cross-browser regression; doc-only edits do not.

rubric.label: Matches regression depth to change blast radius
Avoids wasteful full runs on doc edits

questions.prompt: Why should a regression suite be periodically pruned and audited?

options.text: To retire obsolete/duplicate tests, fix flaky ones, and keep CI fast and trustworthy
To avoid running tests in PRs

questions.explanation: Bloated, flaky suites cause teams to ignore CI failures; curating the suite preserves trust and speed.

questions.prompt: Propose a concise cross-browser and responsive regression matrix for a static GitHub Pages web app targeting Windows 11 primary users and mobile viewports.
questions.explanation: Cover Chromium (Chrome/Edge), Firefox, and WebKit across desktop (1440px) and mobile (360px), focusing E2E on critical journeys and a11y.
